name: Zilpah (Leah's handmaid)
title: Jacob's concubine and mother of two of the tribes of Israel
summary: Zilpah was the handmaid whom Laban gave to his daughter Leah as a gift. When Leah stopped bearing children, she gave Zilpah to Jacob as a concubine, and through her Jacob had two sons: Gad and Asher, who became the ancestors of two of the twelve tribes of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Given to Leah as a handmaid
keyEvents.description: When Leah married Jacob, her father Laban gave her Zilpah as a handmaid.

keyEvents.title: Given to Jacob as a wife
keyEvents.description: When Leah stopped bearing children, she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife so that she might have more children through her.

keyEvents.title: Gad Born
keyEvents.description: Zilpah bore Jacob his seventh son, and Leah named him Gad, which means 'good fortune'.

keyEvents.title: Asher Born
keyEvents.description: Zilpah bore Jacob her second son, and Leah named him Asher, which means 'happy', for she said, 'How happy I am! The women will call me happy.'

keyEvents.title: The Journey to Canaan
keyEvents.description: Zilpah and her sons were part of Jacob's household when they fled from Laban and traveled back to the land of Canaan.
